Two brief EF-0 tornadoes were produced from the same parent circulation as a waterspout came ashore near Rockport, TX. The initial damage as it came on shore was confined to some minor tree damage and a few shingles missing from a couple homes. The tornado then lifted and eventually reformed near FM1781 where it destroyed a couple carports and two sheds. It also snapped some smaller trees and broke numerous large branches before dissipating.

Severe storms spread across South Texas from the Hill Country as a mid-level shortwave replaced a northward lifting warm front over the region. Significant instability, strong DCAPE, and strong shear over 50 knots set up a favorable environment for strong to severe storms with large hail and damaging winds the primary threats. Supercells developed widespread across the area, with large hail reported over the Coastal Plains and Brush Country, an EF-1 tornado was observed in east Calhoun causing damage to several structures and trees. Severe winds also caused significant damage to an RV park south of Port Lavaca, resulting in 2 injuries and at least 12 RVs damaged or completely destroyed.

Kingsville Fire Chief reported several power lines were blown down in the city of Kingsville. Four small grass fires occurred due to the downed power lines.

NWS storm survey determined straight-line winds of approximately 70 to 80 mph struck Belaire Drive in Holiday Beach. The roof was blown off of one home which impacted 2 other homes and caused extensive damage.

NWS Storm survey determined straight-line winds struck a narrow corridor in Fulton between Farm to Market Road 3036 and West Mesquite Street. The winds caused widespread tree damage. A mobile home lost its roof and a metal storage building partially collapsed along Farm to Market Road 1781. An RV was rolled on Circle Drive. Large tree damage was also observed all the way to Fulton Beach Rd. Wind speeds were estimated to be from 70 to 80 mph.

Public and spotter reports of wind gusts between 65 and 75 mph occurred over parts of the city of Corpus Christi east of Staples Street and north of Saratoga Boulevard. The high winds extended northeast toward Texas A & M University at Corpus Christi. Power outages occurred in this section of the city along with minor tree damage.

The strong and damaging winds in Nueces County proceeded across Nueces Bay into San Patricio County. The winds caused utility pole and sign damage as they crossed the Highway 181 Causeway just south of Portland and into the Ingleside community. Numerous trees and branches were blown down in Portland.
Corpus Christi International Airport ASOS measured a gust to 60 mph.
TCOON observation site at Nueces Delta measured a 59 mph wind gust.

NWS storm survey indicated a tornado touched down 5 miles west northwest of Taft along Highway 181. The tornado struck and collapsed a grain elevator. The tornado continued for another couple of miles passing through a subdivision near the intersection of County Road 98 and County Roads 77A and 77B, about 3 miles north northeast of Taft. Tornado touched down in an open farm field 2 miles southeast of Corpus Christi International Airport. The tornado traveled southeast snapping utility poles in front of Clear Channel radio station. It then crossed Old Brownsville Road and destroyed a small RV trailer and damaged a metal building in an adjacent lot.
Winds estimated around 60 mph occurred in Robstown.

Numerous roads flooded in the Portland area including Farm to Market Road 893 at Memorial Parkway.
Numerous roads and intersections flooded in Corpus Christi. Interstate 37 under U. S. Highway 181 and the turnaround near Nueces Causeway was under water.

Spur 202 and Farm to Market Road 3284 were flooded in Gregory. Water depth reached 3 feet in some portions of Gregory. There were 8 families that were rescued from the high water. There were 28 people that were placed in a local shelter due to the flooding. The flood devastated the city of Gregory and the Tradewinds Subdivision 5 miles north of Gregory. In Gregory, 80 percent of the homes were flooded. There were 496 homes with minor damage and 16 homes with major damage. There were 28 businesses in Gregory that received minor damage. In the Tradewinds Subdivision, 26 homes were flooded.
Wind gusts to 60 mph along with pea size hail was reported.
County roads and fields flooded from more than 15 inches of total rainfall.
Street flooding occurred near Highway 77 and Northwest Boulevard.
Funnel cloud was reported east of Kingsville.
Kleberg County official reported tornado near Farm to Market Road 771 east of Riviera. Photo sent to the office confirmed the tornado report.
Vehicles became stranded in flooded roadways around Gregory.
Major street flooding occurred in Portland with water at a depth of 1 to 2 feet flowing down the streets.
Total rainfall of 6.25 inches occurred near Violet Road and Leopard street in Calallen.
Cars were under water in Gregory near Highway 35.
Moore Avenue was impassable between 7 and 8:15 AM due to high water on the road.

NWS storm survey concluded a tornado touched down in an open field south of Highway 35 about 2 miles east of Gregory. The tornado crossed Highway 35 damaging a few power poles. Maximum winds were estimated at 70 mph.

NWS storm survey concluded a tornado touched down in a field south of Highway 35 just east of Gregory. The tornado flipped over a fireworks stand and damaged the side of an outbuilding. The tornado crossed Highway 35 and dissipated in a field. Maximum winds of 70 mph were estimated.
Damage to farm equipment sheds and power lines down northeast of Gregory.
Storm total rainfall of 8.6 inches occurred near Carmel Street.

NWS storm survey concluded a tornado touched down near Lost Creek Drive on the extreme southeast side of Portland. The tornado moved north through the Portland Northshore Country Club producing mainly tree, roof, and fence damage. The tornado moved north into the Bay Ridge subdivision and strengthened. The tornado damaged around 50 homes and several vehicles. Of the homes damaged, 8 received major damage and 15 received minor damage. Maximum sustained winds were estimated to be near 100 mph in this area.
Power outages due to power lines being blown down occurred near Oso Bay to the south of Texas A&M University Corpus Christi campus.
Telephone pole snapped at County Road 79 and Old Robstown Road.
Public reported golf ball sized hail just west of Robstown.
Quarter sized hail occurred just west of the Fairgrounds.
Wind gusts to 60 mph west of Robstown near County Road 83 and Highway 44.
Public reported quarter sized hail at the intersection of Highway 44 and 77 in Robstown.
Public reported quarter sized hail at the Stripes Convenience Store near Interstate 37.

Heavy rain caused street flooding in the central and northwest portions of the city of Corpus Christi. Some roads in rural northwest part of Nueces County had water over the roadways.
A large tree was blown over in Odem with the tree blocking the front door to the house.
High winds blew a tree onto power lines which started a small fire in Sinton.
A highway sign was blown down near mile marker 22 on Interstate 37 near Edroy. A large plastic drum was blown across the interstate.

Winds blew power pole down on to railroad track near Highway 181 northwest of Taft.

Wind gusts over 50 mph occurred in Corpus Christi in association with a wake low pressure area that developed behind the line of thunderstorms. Wind gusts to 58 and 51 mph occurred respectively at Corpus Christi Naval Air Station and Corpus Christi International Airport.

Several roads in and near Sinton were impassable. Water was over the road at various locations along Highways 188 and 234 west of Sinton and Odem, respectively.

Wood roof and awning of home blown completely off. Part of the roof blown into roof of nearby house. One snapped tree limb blown through wall of house. Roof damage and trees uprooted along a two mile path from Live Oak Elementary school to the intersection of Nopal and Austin Streets.
Ping pong ball sized hail occurred in Aransas Pass. Numerous RVs sustained minor to major damage from the hail located at several RV resorts around Aransas Pass.
An NWS employee measured a 59 MPH wind gust in Corpus Christi along South Padre Island Drive.

NWS storm survey team observed 3 mobile homes destroyed at a mobile home park just north of Gregory-Portland High School with several others damaged. Minor damage to moveable bleachers occurred at Gregory-Portland High School with wood and tin debris littering the area. Trees, fences, signs, and power lines were downed on north side of Portland. A barn was destroyed, also. Straight-line winds were estimated to be as high as 100 mph on the northwest side of Portland. Winds of 60 to 70 mph along with marble sized hail produced widespread roof damage to homes throughout Portland.
ASOS at the Corpus Christi International Airport measured a 69 mph wind gust.

Damaging winds occurred from the Calallen area into the Annaville section of Corpus Christi. Metal air vents were bent and damaged at the power station in Calallen. There was sporadic tree, powerline, and fence damage in Calallen. Several metal sheds were destroyed. Trees were snapped and powerlines down in the Annaville area also. Minor to major roof damage occured in this area as well.
Semi truck flipped near the Wal-Mart in Calallen. Street signs were blown and shopping carts were blown onto Highway 77.
Trained spotter reported winds estimated to around 60 mph.
Quarter sized hail occurred in Driscoll.

NWS employee reported trees and powerlines down on the west and north side of Robstown. Shingle and wooden roof damage occurred to homes. The damaging straight-line winds occurred after the tornado moved through the northwest edge of the city.

A National Weather Service (NWS) storm survey team determined a tornado, that touched down 4 miles southeast of Alice International Airport in Jim Wells county continued northeast for 21.5 miles. It travelled through the northwest side of Robstown and ended near Five Points in Calallen. The tornado was strongest from the west-southwest side of Robstown to its end point near Calallen, where wind speeds of up to 100 mph and a width of 200 yards were estimated. Damage to high voltage power lines, poles, large trees, and signs were observed along the path length. In addition, two large sheds, a barn and a tractor were destroyed southwest of Robstown. FM 1069 from State Highway 188 to Business 35 is closed due to high water.
Road closed due to high water on FM 665 from FM 2292 to FM 763. The frontage road on US Highway 77 closed between County Roads 44 and 48.
FM 796 closed due to high water from FM 888 to State Highway 359.

Several roads closed due to flood along Oso Creek. FM 43, FM 763, and FM 2444 closed at Oso Creek. Runoff from heavy rains flowed into Oso Creek which runs along the southwest edge of Corpus Christi. The gaging site on Oso Creek, located on FM 763 about 2 miles west of town, recorded a rapid rise up to 28 feet on Sunday before it stopped working. A post storm survey conducted by the National Weather Service and United States Geological Survey confirmed the creek crested at 30.62 feet around 805 AM Monday morning which beat the previous record of 29.37 feet set in August 1980 during Hurricane Allen.
Area around Weber Road and Yorktown intersection closed.
A 35 year old male drove around a barricade at Weber Road and the flooded Oso Creek. The vehicle was swept 50 yards downstream where he drowned.
Frontage road along Highway 44 about 3 miles west of the Corpus Christi International Airport impassable due to high water. Some of the homes on the north side of the highway were flooded.
Highway 181 and Highway 35 closed due to high water in Gregory. FM 1069 closed North of Ingleside due to water over the roadway.
FM 1944 and FM 631 to Highway 77 to the south of Sinton and east of Odem closed due to high water.
Roads flooded and impassible around the Rockport High School area. Some vehicles needed assistance getting out of the flooded roadways.
Highway 188 closed between Sinton and Interstate 37 with 2 feet of water over portions of the roadway.
Great Lakes Drive in the Lakes subdivision residential area on the south side of Corpus Christi completely covered with water.
FM 1717 east of Highway 77 closed along the intersection with Escondido Creek.
South bound Interstate 37 closed at Carbon Plant Road Underpass. Underpass flooded with cars stalled.
County Road 69 between Robstown and Calallen had over a foot of water over the road.
Intersection of FM 2444 and Highway 286 north of Chapman Ranch under a foot of water.

Flooding across the entire county caused damage to roads and infrastructure. Flooding also damaged a hotel in Aransas Pass with 23 rooms receiving damage. A total of 78 homes were flooded in the cities of Sinton, Ingleside, and Aransas Pass. Sixteen residents in Sinton were evacuated from their homes during the flooding. 17 homes and 3 business were affected by flooding in Ingleside.
The swollen Petronila Creek generated 4 feet of water over County Road 18 between CR 73 and 73B.

Widespread flooding occurred in the Las Colonias subdivision in Corpus Christi. 171 homes received damage from the flooding with 55 homes being considered major and 2 homes destroyed. Flood water depth in the homes ranged from 1/2 foot to 4 feet in this area. One hundred and twenty five residents in the subdivision were rescued and transported to an American Red Cross shelter.
Shelly Blvd. between Ailsie Avenue and General Cavazos Boulevard barricaded due to water over the roadway.

Tranquitas Creek flooded and overflowed 17th Street near the Lee Avenue intersection. 17th Street was barricaded near this intersection. The intersection of 14th Street and King Avenue was barricaded due to high water.
Rainfall amount of 4.5 inches with 2.5 inches in 1 hour between 3 and 4 PM. Water was over the roads but passable.
Rainfall total of nearly 3 inches in the past 8 hours.
Rainfall amounts of 7 inches occurred in the Kings Crossing subdivision with a two day rainfall total at 10.15 inches.
Texas Department of Transportation reported water over the roadway on FM 2826 between County Roads 81 and 85 near Petronila Creek.
Texas Department of Transportation reported water over the road on FM 666 from County Roads 36 to 30.
Bishop Emergency Manager reported flooding occurring within the city.
Law enforcement and spotters reported a funnel cloud over Kingsville near King Avenue.
Spotter reported a funnel cloud near Kingsville.
Spotter reported two funnel clouds east of Bishop.
NWS employee spotted a weak funnel cloud over the south side of Corpus Christi near the intersection of Staples and Yorktown.
Funnel cloud observed over Corpus Christi International Airport for about 10 minutes.

Tree limbs and power lines were down across mainly the western portion of the county. The downed power lines left 1246 customers without power. Peak measured wind gust was 46 mph at McCampbell Airport near Ingleside.

Large trees and power lines were knocked down mainly in the western part of the county causing power outages affecting 6526 customers. The towns of Bishop, Agua Dulce, and Bluntzer were hardest hit. A number of residences suffered damage to carports, fences and trees. Several billboards and a grain elevator were damaged. There were some homes and businesses with minor roof damage. Windows were blown out of the Dairy Queen in Bishop. Peak wind gust of 55 mph was measured at Corpus Christi International Airport. Estimated losses to yield of remaining cotton crop were around a million dollars.

Numerous large tree limbs and power lines were knocked down across the county causing power outages affecting 9437 customers. A roof was blown off of a local business in Kingsville. Minor damage occurred to homes. Peak wind gust measured was 63 mph at Kingsville Naval Air Station.

Storm tides reaching 3.5 feet mean sea level along the coast produced minor flooding along North Padre and Mustang Islands. Water reached the dunes and beach access roads with Beach Access Roads 4, 5, and 6 closed. One vehicle and one camper trailer were flooded on the beach. Tides between 2 and 3 feet in Corpus Christi Bay caused minor flooding on North Beach and Laguna Shores Drive.
Between 2 and 4 inches of rain from Tropical Depression Two produced widespread flooding of secondary County and Farm to Market roads throughout San Patricio County.
Brief funnel cloud observed in Rockport.

Tropical Depression Two produced a storm tide of 2 to 4 feet MSL. Beaches were flooded along Mustang and Padre Islands, and the Padre Island National Seashore was closed. In addition, water from the storm tide was reported over FM 136 in low spots near Bayside.

Between 5 and 8 inches of rain from Hurricane Alex left several flooded County and Farm to Market roadways across San Patricio county for a few days after the event. An elderly couple's vehicle stalled in flood waters near CR 696 & CR 1441. The couple abandoned their vehicle, and swept into floodwaters and drowned.

Between 5 and 8 inches of rain from Hurricane Alex left many creeks, County and Farm to Market roads flooded in western Nueces County. Many low water crossing were flooded along Agua Dulce creek a few days after the event, including crossings at CR 230, 226 and 239. A flood wave from Agua Dulce Creek made it down into Petronila Creeks days after the event, forcing the evacuation of 35 residents from the Fiesta Ranch Colonia near CR 75 and CR 18, southeast of Driscoll. In addition, over 90,000 acres of grain sorghum, 20,000 acres of cotton, 2,000 acres of corn, and 1,500 acres of sunflower and sesame received at least low to moderate damage from the heavy rainfall and flooding.
Wildcat Drive, from Lang Road to Memorial Parkway, was flooded and impassable due to heavy rainfall.
Tornado reported on ground over open country 9 miles NW of Kingsville by a spotter. Location is an estimate. This tornado occurred in the outer rainbands of Hurricane Alex.
A tornado briefly touched down near the intersection of 9th Street and Business 35. Windows were blown out of the Kimco Business. This tornado occurred in the outer rainbands of Hurricane Alex.
City streets in Kingsville became inundated and impassable, due to heavy rainfall.

At the Cove Harbor Marina signs were snapped and roofs partially damaged. Several power lines and trees were reported downed throughout the city of Rockport.

A NWS storm survey team concluded winds of up to 75 mph produced damage consistent with straight-line winds in Aransas Pass. A church had a portion of the roof peeled off. A trailer was also flipped over. Numerous large trees were snapped throughout the city.

A NWS storm survey team of Padre and Mustang Islands estimated winds speeds of up to 90 mph produced wind damage consistent with straight-line winds. Shingles were blown off a bank. On Padre Island a 5 story section of an exterior wall of the Holiday Inn collapsed from the winds. On Mustang Island several large power poles were snapped on Hwy 361, and a large side of a brick wall at the Seagull Condominiums collapsed.

An NWS survey team concluded a tornado touched down 4 miles west of Rockport. The tornado was on the ground for roughly 3.75 miles, traveling southeast and ending near Bypass 35 and 16th streets. The maximum wind speed was estimated at 120 mph, an EF-2, and had a maximum width of almost 3/10 of a mile. Several homes were damaged, an RV flipped, and 4 boats damaged. A home weather station recorded a peak wind gust to 103 mph before failing. Over 20 large tension poles were snapped completely off along Hwy 1069. Hundreds of trees and tree limbs were snapped. Measured at Waldron Field.
Two power poles were snapped at Bravo Street. A large tree and power pole were snapped at Victoria Street.
Lightning struck the Tropical Isles Apartments on Jamaica Drive causing a fire. Time of lightning strike is a rough estimate.

An NWS storm survey team concluded 80-90 mph winds occurred on NAS Corpus Christi, producing damage consistent with straight-line winds. 4 recreational vehicles were flipped and several others moved. 6 people were injured, with one of them receiving critical injuries. Also, debris from a boast barn was blown into the Laguna Madre, and actual boats tossed into a nearby parking lot. The survey team also observed numerous trees damaged or uprooted through NAS Corpus Christi. In addition, one hangar door was blown off its tracks. Finally, the team observed tree and sign damage in Flour Bluff, as well as a car port and roof of a nearby apartment complex damaged.
Two broken power poles on Railroad Street. A stop sign was uprooted along CR 136. Broken power poles were reported at Hwy 181 and CR 3677.

An NWS survey concluded an EF-0 tornado touched down 1/4 mile south of Hwy 286 and CR 18. The tornado was on the ground from roughly 1/2 mile, traveling northeast through crop fields. Width was roughly 10-20 yards wide, base upon crop damage observed. Max wind speeds of 70-80 mph were estimated.

Several hundred large trees and tree limbs snapped throughout the city of Corpus Christi in addition to many power poles. Minor damage was reported to some homes were trees came down on them. Some business signs were blown out. Over 31,000 customers were left without power in Nueces County alone. Debris and brush cleanup by the city went on for weeks after the storm.

Scattered thunderstorms affected portions of South Texas Thursday March 26th 2009. A few of the storms became severe and produced damaging winds, large hail, and frequent lightning. The worst damage was associated with a supercell thunderstorm that developed over central Live Oak County near George West. The supercell moved east-southeast across the extreme southern portion of Bee County into the northern portions of San Patricio County before weakening. This storm produced a 5 to 10 mile swath of damage mainly due to high winds. More information on this severe weather episode can be found at http://www.srh.noaa.gov/crp/stories/Mar2609/default.html.

An NWS Storm Survey Crew found evidence of wind damage along Interstate 37 from mile marker 33 to mile marker 27. Several large trees were down along with large metal highway signs. In addition, an 18 wheeler was flipped near Interstate 37 and Highway 188.

A shallow cold front advanced slowly southward across the Texas Coastal Plains during the afternoon hours. Instability ahead of this boundary increased to nearly 1500 J/KG across the Middle Texas Coastal Plains. A line of strong and severe thunderstorms developed along the cold front from Victoria to Corpus Christi. Steep mid-level lapse rates and cold air aloft supported several storms with hail. Low-level shear supportive of tornadoes was greatest in the vicinity of Corpus Christi, where a tornado did occur.

As a result, rain water seeped into several of the units. A small air conditioning unit was also blown off the roof. Debris from the roof closed Ocean Drive for several hours. Two large tree limbs were also blown down at the Seaside Cemetary. A NWS storm survey was inconclusive as to whether the damage was caused by a small microburst or elevated funnel cloud. Wind speeds were estimated around 55 mph. No other damage was found around this developed intersection.

A weak waterspout moved onshore at Port Aransas as a tornado. The weak tornado produced minor damage before dissipating. Minor damage was reported to a few roofs of residents. Patio furniture and debris was scattered across yards and streets.

EF-0 damage was found along most of the track, however EF-1 damage was found near Arch Street and Spencer Street where the greatest damage occurred with winds of around 100 mph. Between 3 and 5 inches of heavy rainfall resulted in several city streets flooded and impassable throughout Corpus Christi. In addition, Interstate 37 at Corn Products Road was flooded with several feet of water.

Weather conditions along the South Texas Coastal Bend during mid-summer are often conducive to funnel cloud and waterspout development. During the time periods of early to mid morning and late afternoon to early evening, conditions are generally more favorable for the formation of these tropical funnels and weak waterspouts. Instability in the form of early morning thermals within towering cumulus and convection forced later in the day along the seabreeze boundary are the two main mechanisms responsible for these reports.

Mid and upper level winds were relatively light resulting in slow moving and nearly stationary thunderstorms that produced flooding rains. Numerous reports of widespread flooding prevailed across the area with as much as 8-12 inches of rain reported across the greater Corpus Christi metropolitan area.
